features.method: Centre line of the oval CEBAF tunnel, derived from located buildings of the City of Newport News footprint layer, whose building numbers are the lab's own (the list on JLab's site plan, src:geo-jlab-site-plan-detail). (1) Straights: the footprints 'Jefferson Lab #999-01' and '#999-02' ('999 Accelerator Tunnel', labelled twice on the site plan) are two parallel strips 265 m long and 4.5-5 m wide (the tunnel is 'about 14 feet across and 10 feet high'); their axes point 26.4 degrees north of east (bearing 63.6 degrees) and are 160.7 m apart. The straights are drawn along those two axes and extended to the arc tangent points; the North Extractor Service (#21), South Extractor Service (#82) and Injector Service (#53) buildings lie within 1.5 m of the extended lines. (2) Arcs: the eight arc service buildings of the site plan (East Arc Service E2-E5 = #39, #49, #63, #50; West Arc Service W2-W5 = #68, #56, #40, #45) lie on two semicircles. Fitting each semicircle to its three apex buildings (E3-E5, W3-W5) with its centre on the mid-line between the straights gives a radius of 80.3 m, equal to half the straight separation (80.3 m) to within 0.1 m, residuals 0.2-0.6 m (E2 0.2 m, W2 4.4 m); the arcs are therefore drawn as semicircles tangent to both straights, centres 403.4 m apart along the axis. (3) Length: this centre line is 1311 m; the official pages say 'The oval-shaped tunnel is about 7/8 of a mile long' (1408 m): -6.9%, inside the half-step of an eighth-of-a-mile rounding (13/16 to 15/16 mile = 1310 to 1508 m) but not a confirmation of the shape. What is not in the data: the straight lengths beyond the two 265 m strips are inferred from the arc tangent points, and the beam switchyard and hall access tunnels are not drawn. Straights are as located as the city footprints (a few metres); the arcs rest on service buildings that sit on, not necessarily exactly over, the tunnel, so accuracy_m is 20. Haversine on R = 6371008.8 m.
features.name: CEBAF racetrack tunnel centre line (derived from located footprints and arc service buildings)

provenance.locator: City of Newport News Building layer, OBJECTIDs 4572 (#999-01), 81961 (#999-02) and the service-building footprints #39,#49,#63,#50,#68,#56,#40,#45,#21,#82,#53 queried 2026-10-25; JLab site plan list of buildings; jlab.org/node/14330
provenance.note: The shape is computed, not traced: two straights and two semicircles through located buildings. The official length is quoted only as 'about 7/8 of a mile'.

features.method: OpenStreetMap/Nominatim way 246018258 (amenity=research_institute, name 'Thomas Jefferson National Accelerator Facility', address '12000 Jefferson Avenue, Newport News, Virginia 23606'), used verbatim as the campus fence/boundary. Fetched via the Nominatim search API (nominatim.openstreetmap.org) rather than Overpass: both permitted Overpass mirrors (overpass-api.de, lz4.overpass-api.de) refused connections for the entire remainder of this session after an initial handful of successful BNL queries (see worklog); Nominatim, a separate OSM service reading the same underlying database, remained reachable and returns full way geometry via its lookup/search endpoints with 'polygon_geojson=1'. This is still third-party OpenStreetMap data (ODbL) and stays 'approximate', matching every OSM-alone shape in this atlas.

provenance.note: OpenStreetMap alone yields at most 'approximate' confidence (A25). This address (12000 Jefferson Avenue) independently matches Jefferson Lab's own site-plan document ('12 CEBAF Center - 12000 Jefferson Ave.', src:geo-jlab-site-plan-detail), corroborating the identification.

summary.plain: Jefferson Lab's campus in Newport News, Virginia, drawn to scale: the oval underground tunnel of the CEBAF electron accelerator with its two straight sections and two semicircular arcs, the four experimental halls (A to D), the service buildings that stand on the arcs and the other lab buildings. The tunnel outline is derived from the numbered buildings above it, not traced from a map of the tunnel.
